text: Based on the evidence, the 2025 clearing of native forest on this property is likely illegal under Uruguayan law. The 13.5-hectare loss area is confirmed as native forest (13.1 ha) by Uruguay’s Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) 2021 cartography. Uruguay’s Forest Law (Ley 18.435) prohibits the clearing of native forests without prior authorization, and such authorizations are rarely granted for primary or high-conservation-value forests. The JRC 2020 data corroborates that 98% of the area was forested in 2020, supporting its classification as native forest. No legal exemptions (e.g., for planted forests) apply here, as the MGAP data confirms no planted species were present. Thus, the clearing appears to violate national regulations.
